metadata.title: Self-­Regulated Learning in K-­12 School Contexts Shaping Math Achievement: The Influence of Self-­Regulated Learning on East Asian Students in PISA 2022

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2022 microdata with a two-stage stratified random sampling design (schools as primary sampling units, students sampled within schools). It applies PISA sampling weights, explicitly stating the use of W_FSTUWT and replicate/stratification weights W_FSTR1-80, to obtain population-representative estimates and correct standard errors under the complex survey design. The analytic models are estimated separately for each education system (six East Asian economies plus the OECD average) and include ESCS as a covariate. The manuscript does not report any additional preprocessing that would change the weighting scheme (e.g., reweighting after exclusions), so the PISA weights are treated as the primary design correction for cross-system comparisons.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The paper reports the use of PISA’s multiple plausible values for mathematics (PV1MATH–PV10MATH) and sampling weights, but it does not describe how missing questionnaire or covariate data were handled (e.g., whether cases with missing SRL items or ESCS were excluded or imputed). Given that PISA background and questionnaire items can have nontrivial missingness, this omission is a reporting gap that limits reproducibility of the exact analytic sample construction.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The study uses PISA 2022 data for 15-year-old students in six East Asian education systems (Japan, Korea, Hong Kong (China), Macao (China), Singapore, and Chinese Taipei) and compares them with the OECD average. It focuses on the overall mathematics plausible values (PV1MATH–PV10MATH) and constructs two SRL-related indices from specific PISA questionnaire items: learning control and self-monitoring (10 Likert items from ST309) and proactivity toward learning (8 items from ST293 aggregated into MATHPERS). Models are estimated separately for each system and include ESCS as a covariate. The manuscript does not specify additional exclusions (e.g., complete-case rules for SRL items or ESCS), so the filtering beyond the stated SRL index construction and PV selection is not fully documented.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2022 Mathematics (overall PV1MATH–PV10MATH), East Asian systems (Japan, Korea, Hong Kong, Macao, Singapore, Chinese Taipei) vs OECD average
main_findings.target_variable: Learning control & self-monitoring (SRL index from ST309)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Not reported (descriptive cross-system percentages for specific ST309 items; no model fit metrics reported).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2022 mathematics the study examined learning control and self-monitoring behaviours (ST309) across East Asian systems and the OECD average, finding substantial cross-system differences (e.g., higher impulsive responding in Hong Kong and Macao; higher evaluative checking in Korea and Singapore). This indicates that SRL behavioural regulation is not uniformly high across high-performing East Asian systems, suggesting that system-level discipline alone may not guarantee the specific self-monitoring practices linked to deeper learning.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2022 Mathematics (overall PV1MATH–PV10MATH), East Asian systems (Japan, Korea, Hong Kong, Macao, Singapore, Chinese Taipei) vs OECD average
main_findings.target_variable: Proactive learning behaviour (MATHPERS index from ST293)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Not reported (index means with SE reported: Singapore +0.21 (SE=0.01), Chinese Taipei −0.48 (SE=0.02), Japan −0.05 (SE=0.02), Korea −0.13 (SE=0.03), Hong Kong −0.25 (SE=0.02), Macao −0.32 (SE=0.01); OECD average 0.00).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2022 mathematics the study leveraged proactive learning behaviour (MATHPERS from ST293) to compare SRL profiles across East Asian systems and the OECD average, finding Singapore highest and Chinese Taipei lowest relative to the OECD mean. This indicates that proactive engagement varies markedly within the region, implying that policy and pedagogy should target learner agency and proactive study routines rather than assuming they automatically accompany high achievement.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2022 Mathematics (overall PV1MATH–PV10MATH), East Asian systems (Japan, Korea, Hong Kong, Macao, Singapore, Chinese Taipei) vs OECD average
main_findings.target_variable: Mathematics achievement (Plausible Values; quantile regression at 25th and 75th percentiles)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Not reported as model-level metrics; reported effect sizes in score points (e.g., distractibility: −8 points per 1-unit increase in Korea; −6 points in Hong Kong; impulsivity: −12 points per 1-unit increase in Korea and Singapore; −6 points in Macao). Also reported mean achievement gaps by proactive vs less proactive students (e.g., Hong Kong 561 vs 517; Macao 573 vs 525; Chinese Taipei 583 vs 497; OECD 499 vs 454).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2022 mathematics the study leveraged learning control/self-monitoring and proactive learning behaviour to predict mathematics achievement across the performance spectrum (25th vs 75th percentiles), finding that poorer self-regulation (distractibility and impulsivity) is associated with lower achievement and that proactive students score substantially higher than less proactive peers. This indicates that strengthening SRL-oriented instruction (time management, monitoring, and proactive engagement) may improve mathematics outcomes, especially for lower-performing students, though the cross-sectional design prevents causal claims.

data.outcome_summary: This study uses PISA 2022 mathematics data (overall PV1MATH–PV10MATH) to examine how self-regulated learning (SRL) behaviours relate to mathematics achievement across six East Asian education systems (Japan, Korea, Hong Kong (China), Macao (China), Singapore, Chinese Taipei) and the OECD average. It operationalizes SRL using PISA questionnaire items: learning control and self-monitoring from ST309 and proactivity toward learning aggregated into MATHPERS from ST293, while including ESCS as a socioeconomic covariate. The analysis applies quantile regression to compare relationships at the 25th and 75th achievement percentiles and reports descriptive cross-system differences plus score-point associations (e.g., impulsivity: −12 points per 1-unit increase in Korea and Singapore; −6 in Macao; proactive students scoring higher than less proactive peers, e.g., Hong Kong 561 vs 517; OECD 499 vs 454). The manuscript does not report model fit metrics (e.g., R²/AUC) and does not document missing-data handling, limiting reproducibility. Although the study discusses mechanisms, the cross-sectional PISA design means the results should be interpreted as associations rather than causal effects.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The paper is an empirical cross-sectional analysis using quantile regression and descriptive comparisons rather than a machine-learning predictive modeling study; therefore, no ML algorithms (e.g., Random Forest/XGBoost) are evaluated and ml_techniques is left empty. The extraction is still populated with SRL constructs and achievement outcomes, but the schema’s ML-specific fields are not applicable because the methodology does not train or compare ML models.
